issue.title: loop guard does not cover tool-call loops: one session made 1088 successful requests in 5h and counted as 0 loops
issue.body:
## Body

**magpie** v0.1.1546 (Docker, `ghcr.io/yetone/magpie:latest`), provider `trae-cn` via
`@magpie-community/opencode-trae-auth`, endpoint `/v1/messages → /v1/chat/completions`.

### What happened

One client session (`agent=zcode`, a third-party Anthropic-Messages agent on Windows) made **1088
requests** to `group/auto-kimi-k3` in **5 h 08 m** (UTC 07:48:03 → 12:55:36). Every request was
served normally:

| measurement | value |
|---|---|
| requests | 1088 (one session) |
| `status` | 200 × 1088 |
| `stop` | `tool_calls` × 1088 |
| `err` / `rejected` / retries | none |
| input / output | 135,649 / 159,688 |
| cache_read / cache_write | 340,374,528 / 422,383 |
| prompt growth | 139,956 → 431,953 tokens (median +222 per request) |
| `out` token lengths | `149`×356, `152`×233, `103`×231, `106`×153 = **89.4% in 4 values** |

The upstream was healthy the whole time. The problem is that **nothing in magpie noticed**: no
warning, no cap, no entry in the loop counter.

### The gap

`GET /api/usage` (30 d window) on this gateway reports:

```json
{"calls":119019,"errors":1855,"retried":982,"loops":2, ...}
```

**2 loops in 30 days**, against 119,019 calls. This session — 1088 calls, 4.5 h of near-identical
short tool calls — contributes none of them. The existing guard appears to key on text repetition
(the `unitKey` / `runOnWords` / `hasWord` path described in #3594), and a tool-call loop has no
repeating *text*: each response is a structurally identical ~150-token tool call, and the client
re-sends a 140k→432k-token context each turn (only 291,997 tokens of 340M prompt tokens were new,
0.09%).

The session does show up in `GET /api/sessions` with its counts (`calls=1088`, `unpriced=1`,
`transcript=true`), so the data magpie needs is already there — there is just no rule that acts on it.

### Request (bounded, opt-in)

A per-session guard for the *tool-call* shape, independent of the text-repetition guard:

- trip on a configurable combination of (a) requests per session per window and (b) consecutive
  responses whose `stop=tool_calls` count/`out` shape repeats;
- on trip: surface it (UI/API — a `loops`-style field or a warning on `/api/sessions`) and,
  optionally, refuse further requests for that session until the client re-establishes;
- keep it off by default or behind a config switch, and never cut a reply mid-tool-call;
- do not let it replace tool-result handling. A guard must not mask a silently dropped tool result.

Concrete thresholds we would have been happy with: >200 requests in one hour from one session, or
>40 consecutive `tool_calls` responses with no new tool result in the prompt.

### What we are not claiming

- We are **not** claiming magpie caused the loop. Each request was answered correctly.
- We are **not** claiming the tool-result path is broken. Whether the missing results were dropped
  by the client, by magpie's conversion, or upstream is **undetermined**: magpie stores no request
  or response bodies (session recording was off, `/api/sessions/transcript` returned `parts: []`,
  the markdown view says "Nothing was said in this session"), so we cannot compare what the client
  sent against what magpie forwarded.
- The "no new tool result" signal above is derived from magpie's own `prompt.parts[kind=results]`
  item counts in `routing/<date>.jsonl`, not from bodies — so it describes what magpie put in the
  request, not what the client sent.

### Related

- #3594 — loop-guard coverage and bounded recovery (same gap, different shape)
- #2873 — trae-cn plugin: a text-form tool call cut short becomes an error + 60 s backoff
- #3373 — account route drops `tool_use`, so the client never executes the tool

Happy to share the 1088 routing entries (tokens, `stop`, `prompt.parts` shapes) if useful — they
contain no user content.

comments.body:
The gap is that the tool loop guard only read turns that had results. `exchanges`/`exchangeOf` in `internal/gateway/tool_loop.go` stop at a turn with no tool result, and `mayLoop` parsed only a body holding 8 tool results, so a conversation whose turns are the same call with nothing answering it was never read at all. That is the shape your 1088 entries describe: every reply a ~150-token tool call, the prompt growing by the call alone, no tool result ever added.

The branch reads that shape too. `toolLoopUnansweredOf` walks the request's own messages back from the newest and counts the calls asked in a row with no result after them, same name and arguments, call ids ignored. Eight in a row answer the turn here, in the agent's own protocol, with a notice that says the result never came back (nothing claims the call did not run), and the turn goes nowhere. The Routing view and the usage row are the existing `Tool loop stopped` / `tool loop:` rejection, so `/api/sessions` and Usage show it. A turn asking a different call, a reply that says something else, a result, or a word from the user starts the count again. No new setting and no new string: Settings › Models › Replies › *Stop looping replies* turns it off with the reply guard.

[fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover), commit 125a5e087ef882a6223dff6645589b0ee33cdbd6

Run: `TestToolLoopStuckWithoutResults` fails before the change on all eight protocol cases (Responses streamed and whole, Codex's own path, Chat streamed and whole, Anthropic streamed and whole, Gemini) with the vendor's reply reaching the agent, and passes after, the vendor asked 0 times; 7 turns go on. `TestToolLoopStuckNeedsTheSameCallAndNoWord` holds the progress cases. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/gateway/`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/gateway/` and `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -run 'TestToolLoop'` are clean. The full `internal/gateway` suite was run once and failed only in five tests that fail the same way on clean `upstream/main` (`TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget`, `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw`'s `\u2028` escaping, `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`); a second full-suite run at the committed head was not completed.

This is a fork branch, ready to review, and not a claim on the issue. It does not add the per-session windowed cap or a refusal for the session, which you also floated: those need a new setting and per-session state, so that part is left to the maintainer.

Yielding to @skygunner's branch — I took this issue earlier only to verify their fix independently, and it verifies. No patch from me; this is a verification endorsement.

## Mechanism, claim by claim

| skygunner's claim | What the code does | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| The guard only read turns that had results: `exchanges`/`exchangeOf` stop at a turn with no tool result, and `mayLoop` parsed only a body holding 8 tool results | True of `upstream/main` before this branch; the ablation below reproduces the gap (8/8 red) | yes |
| `toolLoopUnansweredOf` walks the request's own messages back from the newest and counts the calls asked in a row with no result after them, same name and arguments, call ids ignored | Key is `Name + "\x00" + steadyArgs(Args)` (argument key order normalized, `ID` never read); a non-assistant message carrying parts (a result or a word from the user) breaks the walk; a turn asking a different call breaks it; a reply that says something breaks it; a reasoning-only turn in between does not | yes |
| Eight in a row answer the turn in the agent's own protocol, with a notice that says the result never came back (nothing claims the call did not run), and the turn goes nowhere | The `unanswered` branch of `why()`/`notice()` says "no result came back" / "never sent back a result … nothing says whether the call ran"; the turn exits through the existing `answeredHere` path, so the Routing trace is the same "Tool loop stopped" and the usage row is provider `magpie`, rejected, error starting `tool loop:` (the test asserts all of it) | yes |
| No new setting and no new string: Settings › Models › Replies › Stop looping replies turns it off with the reply guard | No settings/GUI/i18n change; the notice text is in-agent, not a GUI string; the off switch is the existing `noLoopGuard` | yes |
| `mayLoop` reads a body with 8 tool calls as well as 8 tool results, matched loosely | `toolCallMarks` counted alongside `toolResultMarks`; a mark that also matches a result only costs an extra parse, it cannot change the verdict (the verdict is `toolLoopOf`/`toolLoopUnansweredOf`, both reading parsed messages) | yes |

## Verification (all run locally on darwin/arm64, tip `e17b6cefc`)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 3-way am of `125a5e08` onto current `upstream/main` tip | Applied; one conflict, and it is a side-by-side addition: tip has since added the wait/poll exemption (`allWaits`/`isWait`, "a turn whose calls are all waits is never a loop") at the same spot. Both blocks kept, the fix's semantics untouched |
| `TestToolLoopStuckWithoutResults` (RED before, GREEN after) | RED: with `tool_loop.go` reverted to tip and the test kept, all 8 protocol subtests fail with exactly "the agent wasn't told of the loop in its API" — the vendor's reply reaching the agent. GREEN after: 8/8 subtests pass (Responses stream + whole, Codex, Chat stream + whole, Anthropic stream + whole, Gemini), 7 turns go on, the 8-turn turn stops with the vendor asked 0 times, usage row `magpie`/rejected/`tool loop … no result` |
| `TestToolLoopStuckNeedsTheSameCallAndNoWord` | Passes: differing arguments pass through, a word from the user between the calls passes through |
| Full `-run 'TestToolLoop'` set on the am'd tip | 40 tests, 0 failures (including tip's own `TestToolLoopLetsWaitsBy`, so the wait exemption survives beside the new check) |
| Full package `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/gateway/` | **Clean: exit 0, 0 failures, 706s.** The five base-reds in the branch's own notes (`TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget`, `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, `FuzzMarshalRaw`'s `\u2028` escaping, `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`) did not reproduce on today's tip on this machine — that second full run their notes left unfinished is now done, green |
| Reset conditions | Pinned by tests for differing arguments and a user's word; a **result** resetting the count has no dedicated test case — I pinned it with a throwaway white-box probe (a result after turn 4 of 10 resets; alternating names never count as one call; differing call ids are ignored; a reasoning turn in between does not reset; 7 turns stay under the threshold). All pass |
| Over-blocking edge (legit repeated same-name calls) | A retry or poll only counts when its result never comes back *and* the arguments are byte-identical: any result resets the count, any argument difference resets it, and tip's `allWaits` exemption already covers answered waits in the result-shaped check. Only a client that asks the same call 8 times and sends back no result at all is stopped — that is the #3615 shape itself. One observation for the maintainer: the unanswered check has no wait exemption, so `sleep(60s)` asked 8 times with results never sent back would stop too; the wait exemption's premise ("answered the same by design") does not hold in that shape, and a normal client always sends a wait's result back, so I do not read this as a defect — leaving it as a recorded observation |
| `gofmt -l` (both touched files, also via `tr -d '\r'`) | Clean |
| `go vet ./internal/gateway/` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/gateway/` | Both clean |
| Freshness | `upstream/main` has no commit mentioning 3615; not merged yet |

Branch: [skygunner/magpie `fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover) (head `125a5e087ef882a6223dff6645589b0ee33cdbd6`)

Not verified: a real zcode session against the reporter's 1088 routing entries (not available; the fixtures carry the shape their numbers describe), and Windows itself.

Thanks @easonlao for the report and @skygunner for the fix branch.

AI use: verification performed with AI assistance; all commands and outputs above were run and read locally.

补充一个相关但不完全相同的案例：**工具已执行且有成功结果记录，但 Agent 反复核验／改写收尾说明，任务不再实质推进**。希望讨论现有循环保护的覆盖边界，以及可选的会话级止损。关联 #1858。

### 环境与证据范围

- Windows，Codex Desktop 经 Magpie 执行每日简报任务。Codex 会话日志中的 `cli_version` 为 `0.167.0-alpha.4.1`，不是桌面应用版本号。
- 会话配置模型标签为 `myh/gpt-6-astra`；这只是客户端路由标签，不是对实际 served model 或底层模型身份的验证。
- 事后只读核对 Magpie 配置，`noLoopGuard` 字段不存在（未显式关闭）；这不能证明事发时该请求实际经过了哪一版检测器。Magpie 事发版本和对应 route ID 尚未核实。
- 下列统计来自本地 Codex 原始 JSONL，**仅统计 2026-11-13 08:24:08—09:00:33（UTC+8）的一个任务轮次**，排除了后续用户追问。没有上传原始会话、私有文档、路径或密钥。

### 实际观察

| 项目 | 日志结果 |
|---|---:|
| 本轮耗时 | 约 36 分 25 秒 |
| `web_search_call` 事件 | 47 次：两个相同页面目标分别出现 5 次、42 次 |
| 本地面板技术交付完成时间 | 08:33:02；此时来源审计仍未通过，不等于整项任务完成 |
| 技术交付后仍发生的网页工具事件 | 36 次 |
| 技术交付后追加的本地命令调用 | 37 次；反复写运行记忆／事故说明／验证记录，37 个结果均记录退出码 0 |
| 本轮累计输入 Token | 7,348,639，其中缓存输入 6,973,766 |
| 本轮累计输出 Token | 76,760 |
| 本轮累计总 Token | 7,425,399 |
| 08:33:02 之后增加的累计总 Token | 5,605,699，约占本轮 75.5% |

本轮没有发现上下文压缩事件。工具事件数不等于 Magpie 上游 HTTP 请求数；Token 是客户端累计统计，包含缓存输入，不能按未缓存单价直接推算费用。网页事件记录也不能证明网页内容成功获取。

Agent 多次声称“此前没有真正调用，现在才是第一次／唯一一次”，但事件日志中同一页面已出现大量重复调用。各次脚本、说明措辞和时间戳会变化，循环在语义层面相似，而非所有工具名称、参数与输出都逐字相同。

### 与本 issue 已讨论修复的区别

这里**至少在客户端日志中有成功的工具结果**，并不是已经证实的“连续同名同参数调用且始终没有结果回传”。因此不能直接假定修复 unanswered-tool-call 检测就能覆盖本例，也不能只凭客户端日志证明下一次上游请求完整保留了工具历史。

我没有据此认定 Magpie 导致循环，或断言工具结果在某一层丢失。要定位还需比较脱敏后的“工具实际响应 → 客户端下次请求 → 网关转发内容”。当前反馈重点是：**成功返回、参数变化、反复核验却无实质进展的循环，有没有独立的止损机制？**

### 希望考虑的保护（可选开启）

1. **会话／任务轮次级硬预算**：请求次数、时间窗口、累计消耗达到用户阈值时警告或在下一次请求入口拒绝继续；与精确重复检测独立。支持显式恢复，避免客户端自动重试不断刷新限额。费用、未缓存输入和缓存读取分别展示，计入哪些 Token 应可配置。
2. **近似重复／无进展提示**：对同一目标反复读取、核验、改写总结的模式提供可解释警告；不把“命令 exit 0”直接当成任务进展。语义判定应可选，并避免误伤正常轮询、测试和调试；若网关看不到任务状态，可明确需要 Agent 提供阶段／进展信号，而不是声称已判断任务完成。
3. **可观测的停止原因**：记录会话标识、实际 served provider/model、触发规则、计数、预算及 action；区分普通回复重复、精确工具循环、疑似无进展和预算超限。只限制实际经过该网关的请求，不声称能停止客户端独立执行的命令或原生网页工具。

理解网关不能安全回滚 Agent 历史或工作区；本反馈不要求自动撤销文件或健康检查点恢复。如果已有设置能覆盖，请指出入口和所需版本；如果应另开 feature issue，也请告知。

### 与本 issue 已讨论修复的区别

这里**至少在客户端日志中有成功的工具结果**，并不是已经证实的“连续同名同参数调用且始终没有结果回传”。因此不能直接假定修复 unanswered-tool-call 检测就能覆盖本例，也不能只凭客户端日志证明下一次上游请求完整保留了工具历史。

我没有据此认定 Magpie 导致循环，或断言工具结果在某一层丢失。要定位还需比较脱敏后的“工具实际响应 → 客户端下次请求 → 网关转发内容”。当前反馈重点是：**成功返回、参数变化、反复核验却无实质进展的循环，有没有独立的止损机制？**

### 希望考虑的保护（可选开启）

1. **会话／任务轮次级硬预算**：请求次数、时间窗口、累计消耗达到用户阈值时警告或在下一次请求入口拒绝继续；与精确重复检测独立。支持显式恢复，避免客户端自动重试不断刷新限额。费用、未缓存输入和缓存读取分别展示，计入哪些 Token 应可配置。
2. **近似重复／无进展提示**：对同一目标反复读取、核验、改写总结的模式提供可解释警告；不把“命令 exit 0”直接当成任务进展。语义判定应可选，并避免误伤正常轮询、测试和调试；若网关看不到任务状态，可明确需要 Agent 提供阶段／进展信号，而不是声称已判断任务完成。
3. **可观测的停止原因**：记录会话标识、实际 served provider/model、触发规则、计数、预算及 action；区分普通回复重复、精确工具循环、疑似无进展和预算超限。只限制实际经过该网关的请求，不声称能停止客户端独立执行的命令或原生网页工具。

理解网关不能安全回滚 Agent 历史或工作区；本反馈不要求自动撤销文件或健康检查点恢复。如果已有设置能覆盖，请指出入口和所需版本；如果应另开 feature issue，也请告知。
